questions.q: When the apostles at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them. What specific action did Peter and John take upon arrival? (Acts 8:14-17)
options: They collected tithes from the new believers.
They appointed seven deacons for the Samaritans.
They prayed for them and laid their hands on them so they might receive the Holy Spirit.
They commanded them to relocate to Jerusalem.
questions.explain: The Samaritans had only been baptized in the name of Jesus, so Peter and John "prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit... Then they laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Spirit."

questions.q: As Peter was preaching the gospel in the house of Cornelius, what astonishing event caused the circumcised believers who came with Peter to be amazed? (Acts 10:44-46)
options: The house was suddenly filled with gold coins.
The Holy Spirit fell on the Gentiles, and they began speaking in tongues and praising God.
Cornelius resigned from the Roman army instantly.
Fire came down from heaven and consumed a sacrifice.
questions.explain: The Jewish believers were amazed because the gift of the Holy Spirit was poured out even on the Gentiles, proving God's acceptance of them as evidenced by their speaking in tongues.

questions.q: When Peter defended his decision to eat with uncircumcised Gentiles before the Jerusalem church, what was his concluding argument that silenced his critics? (Acts 11:17)
options: "I am the head apostle, and you must obey me without question."
"The Gentiles offered me money that will help the poor in Jerusalem."
"If God gave the same gift to them as he gave to us when we believed, who was I that I could stand in God's way?"
"The Roman governor forced me to go to his house."
questions.explain: Peter recounted the events and concluded that God had sovereignly chosen to save the Gentiles, saying, "If then God gave the same gift to them as he gave to us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I that I could stand in God's way?" Hearing this, they glorified God.

questions.q: When Peter arrived in Joppa where the beloved disciple Dorcas had died, what were the widows in the upper room doing? (Acts 9:39)
options: They were cooking a large funeral feast.
They were weeping and showing him tunics and other garments that Dorcas made while she was with them.
They were singing joyful hymns.
They were preparing to bury her in a nearby cave.
questions.explain: Acts 9:39 says, "All the widows stood beside him weeping and showing tunics and other garments that Dorcas made while she was with them." This highlighted her life of good works.

questions.q: After Peter's miraculous release from prison (Acts 12), he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark. Who answered the door and was so overjoyed that she left him standing outside?
options: Martha
Lydia
Rhoda
Sapphira
questions.explain: Acts 12:13-14 states: "And when he knocked at the door of the gateway, a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer. Recognizing Peter's voice, in her joy she did not open the gate but ran in and reported that Peter was standing at the gate."
